a total of 154 compounds (including aldehydes, esters and polyphenols) were identified and quantified in oaked Chardonay wine samples by HS-SPME GC/MS, and 1H-NMR spectroscopy.
the oxidation of oaked wines during long-term storage can be monitored by a combination of HS-SPME and 1H-NMR.

the identification of new markers of wine oxidation, and the elucidation of chemical reactions involved in the oxidation process.
the development of an integrated analytical strategy based on HS-SPME/GC-MS and 2D NMR spectroscopy to study the evolution of wine oxidation compounds during long-term storage.

the development of an analytical strategy for the assessment of oxidation compounds and their correlation with browning index, which could be useful for the monitoring of wine oxidation during storage.

this study provides an extensive characterization of oaked wine oxidation, which will be of great value for the wine industry.

the HS-SPME GC/MS and 13C NMR metabolomics approaches were able to provide a detailed profile of wine compounds and their variation in response to oxidation, and that the combination of these two techniques can be a valuable tool for the study of wine oxidation.
the HS-SPME/GC-MS and 2D 1H-NMR approaches are complementary and powerful tools for the analysis of oaked Chardonnnay wine oxidation.

the combination of GC-MS and NMR metabolomics is an efficient tool to identify and characterize the compounds that are formed during the aging of oaked white wines, which can be used to develop predictive models of wine aging.
